title: Your AI just moved out of the cloud

lines: Every time you ask an AI something, your words leave your laptop.
As of October sixteenth, they don't have to.
Today, your question flies to a data center,
waits in line on someone else's computer,
and the answer flies all the way back.
That's the lag. That's the subscription.
And that's your private files, out for a ride.
NVIDIA's RTX Spark puts a data center chip inside a laptop.
Twenty Grace CPU cores, built with MediaTek.
Six thousand one hundred forty-four Blackwell GPU cores.
Up to one petaflop of AI math.
On paper, that's a million billion calculations, every second.
But the real trick isn't speed. It's memory.
A gaming laptop splits its memory in two.
Here, both chips share one pool, up to a hundred and twenty-eight gigabytes.
NVIDIA says that runs AI models with a hundred and twenty billion parameters, right on your lap.
The catch? It's an Arm chip.
Older Windows apps run through a translator called Prism.
And it starts at two thousand five hundred ninety-nine dollars.
Six brands are selling them now.
Your next AI might not live in the cloud.
It might live right here.
